anchors.description: Straight-line distance along one horizontal brick course on the brick spandrel wall left of the mesh gate, between two vertical mortar joints that span three full stretcher bricks
anchors.visible_evidence: Running-bond brickwork with clear courses and staggered vertical joints; three full stretcher pitches counted between the two marked joints; observed course-pitch vs stretcher-pitch ratio (~8 px : ~19 px, about 1:2.4) matches a standard ~250 x 90 mm clay brick with recessed mortar joints
anchors.identity_uncertainty: Brick format not legible; span would be about 0.72 m with a 240 mm unit and 0.81 m with a 270 mm unit; endpoints placed within about 2 px of the joint centres

anchors.description: Outer width of the steel-mesh pedestrian gate leaf carrying the green emergency-exit sign, measured between the outer faces of the two vertical frame tubes at the top rail
anchors.visible_evidence: Gate leaf has a clear rectangular frame (top rail plus both vertical tubes) and the leaf outline is about 1:2 width:height, matching 1.0 m wide x ~2.0 m high standard mesh gates; about 18-20 vertical mesh modules across the leaf are consistent with 50 mm mesh over roughly 1 m
anchors.identity_uncertainty: No product label; could be a 1.2 m gate leaf or a 0.9 m door leaf; width is taken between outer frame edges, so viewing angle does not change the physical span
